Win_Loss_Reason: Strong product fit and executive sponsorship
Notes: Customer had been evaluating us for 6 months. Key differentiator was our API integration capabilities and 24/7 support SLA. Champion was VP of Engineering Sarah Chen who drove internal adoption. Competitor ServiceNow was in final round but lost on flexibility and total cost of ownership. Implementation timeline was aggressive but we committed to 90-day go-live.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Textbook enterprise sale. Champion identified early, multi-threaded across 4 stakeholders. POC was decisive moment - our platform processed their 2M daily transactions without issues. Pricing was competitive at $37.50/user/month vs ServiceNow at $45/user.

Notes: Lost to HubSpot after 3-month evaluation. Customer felt our pricing was 40% higher for comparable features. Key gap was native marketing automation - they needed email campaigns built-in rather than through integration. Decision maker CFO pushed back on ROI timeline showing 18-month payback vs HubSpot's 9-month projection. Our champion (Director of Sales) tried to push through but was overruled.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: We entered this deal late and never recovered positioning. Should have led with ROI calculator earlier. Missing marketing automation module cost us - this is the 3rd deal this quarter lost to HubSpot on this gap. Need product roadmap response.

Notes: Large digital transformation initiative across 12 European factories. Currently in contract negotiation phase. Key stakeholders aligned on our platform but procurement is pushing for 25% discount. Competitor SAP has existing ERP relationship but customer wants modern cloud-native approach. Risk: CTO retirement in Q2 could delay decision. Budget approved by board in November.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Largest deal in EMEA pipeline. Multi-year contract with $1.2M Year 1 and $800K recurring. Need to close before CTO transition. Legal review of data residency requirements for EU operations in progress. SAP is incumbent but our cloud-native architecture is the differentiator.

Notes: Won after competitive bake-off against Oracle Retail and Shopify Plus. Customer operates 200+ retail locations across Australia and New Zealand. Our POS integration with their existing inventory management system was the deciding factor. Implementation includes real-time analytics dashboard for store managers. Champion: Head of Digital Commerce Lisa Park.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Clean win driven by technical superiority in the bake-off. Oracle couldn't match our real-time sync capabilities. Shopify Plus lacked enterprise features for multi-location management. Customer referenced our ANZ retail case studies as confidence builders.

Notes: Lost after 4-month evaluation. Customer's compliance team raised concerns about our data sovereignty approach - they require all data to remain in Canadian data centers. Our current infrastructure uses US-based primary servers with Canadian replication. Competitor Temenos won with their Canadian-first deployment model. Despite strong technical evaluation scores, the compliance requirement was non-negotiable.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: This loss highlights our infrastructure gap in Canada. Third financial services deal lost on data sovereignty this year. Need urgent discussion with infrastructure team about Canadian primary deployment option. The technical team loved our product but compliance had veto power.

Notes: Healthcare patient portal for 15 hospitals across Scandinavia. Currently in proposal stage after successful POC. Key requirements: HIPAA-equivalent compliance (EU health data regulations), integration with Epic EHR systems, and patient-facing mobile app. Competition is from local vendor Cambio Healthcare. Our advantage: proven Epic integration track record and mobile-first architecture.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Strong technical fit but facing local vendor preference. Need to emphasize our Nordic reference customers and EU data compliance certifications. The POC showed 3x faster patient portal load times vs their current system. Budget committee meets in March.

Notes: Won against Salesforce Field Service and ServiceMax. Customer has 500+ field technicians servicing solar installations. Our offline-capable mobile app was the decisive factor - technicians often work in areas with poor connectivity. The ability to sync work orders and capture signatures offline then auto-sync when connected was unique to our platform. 6-month implementation plan with phased rollout.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Niche win leveraging our offline-first mobile architecture. This is a growing segment - renewable energy field service. The customer plans to expand to 1000 technicians in 2 years which would double the contract value. Good reference account for the energy vertical.

Notes: Early-stage discovery for AI-powered supply chain optimization across Southeast Asia operations. Customer manages 50,000+ SKUs across 8 countries. Initial conversations with CTO reveal strong interest in predictive demand forecasting and automated reorder points. No formal evaluation process yet. Key risk: customer has historically built internal tools and may choose to build vs buy. Budget not yet allocated.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Massive opportunity but very early stage. Customer is a tech-forward logistics company that could become a flagship APAC reference. Need to demonstrate clear ROI vs build-in-house option. Suggest executive sponsorship program and custom POC focused on their top 3 pain points.

Notes: Lost to incumbent vendor Guidewire after extended evaluation. Customer's existing Guidewire implementation created significant switching costs. Despite our platform demonstrating 40% faster claims processing in POC, the estimated $2M migration cost and 18-month timeline made the business case difficult. Key learning: should have partnered with a migration specialist to reduce perceived risk.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: Classic incumbent lock-in loss. Our product was technically superior but the migration risk was too high for the customer. Need to develop a Guidewire migration accelerator toolkit to address this recurring blocker. This is the second UK insurance deal lost to Guidewire migration concerns.

Notes: IoT sensor monitoring platform for copper mining operations in Chile and Peru. Customer wants real-time equipment health monitoring to prevent unplanned downtime. Initial qualification meeting went well - they're spending $5M annually on unplanned maintenance. Our IoT platform with predictive analytics could reduce that by 30-40%. Next step: technical workshop with their operations team in Santiago.
Deal_Review_Notes: Deal review: New vertical opportunity in LATAM. Mining IoT is underserved and this could be a beachhead account. The ROI story is compelling - $5M maintenance spend with 30% reduction potential means $1.5M savings vs our $780K contract. Need domain expertise support from our industrial IoT team.
